description.value: A developed BC Parks campground on a large, deep Cariboo lake with a roped swimming beach, rainbow trout fishing, and rentable canoes amid old-growth cedars; the 65 km access from Hwy 97 is mostly paved with a final 10 km of well-maintained gravel.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The BC Parks website confirms Horsefly Lake Park is an active provincial campground with a 23-site frontcountry campground plus 7 walk-in sites operated by Silvertip Park Services Ltd. The site details activities, facilities (beach with change rooms, hiking trail), and access (65 km from 150 Mile House, last 10 km gravel), but does not address most cyclist-specific amenities such as potable water, showers, or food storage. The prominent 'Book camping' function on the BC Parks page, combined with the frontcountry camping subpage describing the reservation system, confirms reservations are accepted.
concerns: OSM name is 'Horsefly Lake' but the official BC Parks name is 'Horsefly Lake Park' — minor naming discrepancy.
Final 10 km of access road is gravel, which may be a practical barrier for road-touring cyclists.
OSM phone number (+1-250-320-9305) is attributed to park operator Silvertip Park Services Ltd.; it is not directly listed on the park webpage visited, so confirmation is indirect.
No sani-station within the park; website notes community sani-station services are available nearby but does not specify location.
No street address available in OSM or on the website.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A legitimate, active BC Parks provincial campground with 23 drive-in plus 7 walk-in sites; the walk-in capacity and remote lakeside setting make it a viable stop for self-supported touring cyclists exploring the Cariboo backcountry.
enrichment_extras.notes: OSM capacity tag ('23 + 7 walk-in') indicates 7 walk-in sites that may be accessible to cyclists arriving without a vehicle, though the website does not label them as hiker/biker sites. OSM tag internet_access=no is consistent with the BC Parks frontcountry camping page noting most parks lack internet connectivity.

wow_evidence: roped swimming beach, rainbow trout fishing, and rentable canoes amid old-growth cedars
